children: Anthropic (ANT) CEO Dario Amodei said on Wednesday that AI could lead to job losses and that it would make sense to pace development to allow workers to adapt to the changes.
Many tech companies have cut jobs in recent years as AI-driven efficiencies reduce the need for certain roles, while shifting their focus toward AI-powered products and services.
AI's rapid development has also raised questions about whether existing safeguards and regulations can keep pace with the technology's growing capabilities, prompting calls to slow its development.

"In some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt," Amodei said in an X post on Wednesday.
In the lengthy post, Amodei said he has consistently advocated for democratic oversight of AI and warned against sacrificing human “self-determination” for efficiency or security.

He also highlighted concerns around “recursive self-improvement” (RSI), warning that allowing AI to build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision could make systems advance faster than humans can control.

Amodei said decisions about AI automation should be distributed among governments, companies, society, and individuals, rather than resting with a single decision-maker. "AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process," he wrote.
Tech Layoffs Continue
The cuts at tech companies come against a broader backdrop of AI- and automation-led job reductions.
Last month, Microsoft
it was offering buyouts to reportedly 60,000 workers worldwide, after eliminating about 4,800 jobs in July.

Before that, Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate roles in January, though the company framed the reductions around reducing managerial layers and bureaucracy. Coinbase laid off about 700 employees in May.
The tech sector has seen 149,158 tech employees laid off at 364 companies this year, according to Layoffs.fyi.
ANT Stocks Pops
rose 1.1% on Wednesday and a further 1.8% in overnight trading, returning to green for the first time since its IPO debut rally last Thursday.
ANT stock was at $84.27 at the time of writing, above its $83 IPO price.
Cathie Wood Buys More ANT Stock
Ace investor Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management bought 317,053 shares of Anthropic across its six funds on Wednesday, valued at about $26.2 million.
Wood
a $62-million lot the previous day and has been aggressively loading up ANT shares since the AI lab’s IPO last week.
Retail View For ANT
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for ANT dipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish.’
“$AND average down every small dip. This is going to fly. $300 easy,” said a trader, while another wrote: “$ANT bought some today to hold for a while.”
Anthropic shares rose 1.1% on Wednesday and a further 1.8% in overnight trading, climbing above its $83 IPO price.
Cathie Wood’s ARK purchased $26.2 million worth of ANT shares.
Retail sentiment for ANT dipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish,’ though many traders said they bought shares.

title: Anthropic CEO Flags AI Job Risks, Says Deployment Should Be Paced To ‘Give People More Time To Adapt’
